# Grid: opt-in content-sized rows for buffered flat data

Terminal predicate: Buffered flat grids can opt into content-sized wrapped-text rows while preserving visible-record stability, aligned bodies within one view, keyboard navigation and final-row reachability; independent views at different widths keep independent geometry.

## Problem scope

Fixed-height buffering uses index-times-height offsets and fixed-height extents. Wrapped text needs different heights, but absolute row positioning, recycled cells, split bodies and painted scroll acknowledgement must still agree.

This epic coordinates one geometry contract with its native measurement, buffering, scrolling and navigation consumers, then the actual Grid journey proving that outcome. A helper or scrollbar-only patch cannot establish it. The first delivery is a bounded text-only PoC with declared height-driving columns over fully loaded flat data. Fixed height remains the default.

The design graduated from [D#19645](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19645), accepted body SHA-256 `5c5c9d62cd99a2ad90dd3cf8362862f1a2bb6e64a7967b6137b8bc4e8a11459f`. The operator-directed [supersession record](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/9495#issuecomment-6125603246) closed #9495 and calls for this fresh epic. The historical research remains linked there; all-active-window synchronization remains deferred under #9486.

## Intended solution

The App Worker owns one geometry model per view, keyed by record and layout context. It supplies cumulative row offsets, inverse offset lookup, pixel-based buffered coverage and both Body/proxy scroll extents. Synchronized bodies inside that view use the maximum height of its declared wrapping text columns; separate views do not share a scalar height merely because they show the same record.

Use Neo's existing native browser paths: measure displayed block text containers in place, and pre-render unmounted rows or horizontally unmounted height-driving columns in the Grid's style scope at their actual widths. Reuse the render/rect transport. Known rows use measured sizes; unseen rows use estimates refined from available measurements. A plain prefix array is the initial index candidate.

Content, width, column and font/theme changes invalidate the applicable context. Responses carry record/view/layout generation and cannot update recycled records or older layouts. Scroll corrections reconcile with the pinning addon's acknowledged origin. Navigation, including `Body.scrollToIndex`, consumes the same geometry. `AnimateRows` must either consume it or expose an explicit incompatibility in this opt-in mode; silent fixed-height arithmetic is not accepted.

Work belongs in the Grid's existing owners (`src/grid/{Body,Row,View,VerticalScrollbar}`, the Grid cell SCSS and affected Grid consumers), reusing `DomAccess.getLayoutRect`/`getNaturalRect` and the `MagicMoveText` render/measure pattern. New module placement, if needed, is decided in implementation intake rather than prescribed as a new service here.

The source Discussion records the exact-source census, scratch measurements and fixed-grid wheel receipt. These justify a bounded implementation experiment; they do not establish integrated dynamic-row performance. Actual measurement scheduling, parity, generation races, scrolling and final-row reachability remain required implementation evidence.

## Deferred scope and avoided traps

Arbitrary image/component/stateful renderer sizing, TreeStore population semantics, remote/partial datasets, uniform N-line presets, capped automatic rows, scaled scrolling beyond tested native extents and all-active-window synchronization are outside this PoC.

No third-party line breaker, second worker typography authority, general measurement service or Fenwick tree is required. A constrained outer row is not a natural-content oracle; a measured average does not replace known heights or prove an exact unseen total. Main-thread measurement supplies observations; the App Worker owns geometry and within-view body alignment.

Before tracked implementation, coordinate overlapping Grid/navigation files with #19515 and the header-menu work in #19643. Their existing outcomes and owners remain independent.

I took part in D#19645 ([18880377](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19645#discussioncomment-18880377), [18880598](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19645#discussioncomment-18880598), [18880809](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19645#discussioncomment-18880809), [18881069](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19645#discussioncomment-18881069)), so this follows the participant path: Stages 1–2 cite my positions, and Stages 3–5 run in full on Euclid's transformation of the Discussion into this epic.

Drives `Row` offsets and heights, `View.syncBodies`, pixel pool coverage, both extents (`Body` and `VerticalScrollbar`) and `Body.scrollToIndex`. Heights come first from a **synthetic height function**, so geometry is testable before measurement exists. Fixed height is the control. | — |
| **L2 — content-sized cells + in-place measurement** | The block text container CSS (see Stage 4), plus batched `getLayoutRect` of mounted containers with padding/border added and the row maximum taken across bodies. A record/view/layout generation fence rejects stale responses. | L1 |
| **L3 — hidden pre-render + measure-ahead** | A `visibility:hidden` subtree in the grid's style scope at actual widths, for unmounted rows and off-screen height-driving columns. Measures about one pipeline-latency beyond the overscan, refines in idle time, estimates unseen rows from the measured mean, and invalidates on font arrival. | L2 |
| **L4 — scroll stability** | Anchor correction through the pinning addon's acknowledged origin; extent changes held during a thumb drag and settled at release; the pinning-order race spec; final-row reachability before and after settlement. | L1 |
| **L5 — `AnimateRows`** | Consumes the geometry model in this mode, or rejects the combination explicitly. | L1 |
| **L6 — the acceptance journey** | A wrapped-text example (100k rows, locked columns so all three bodies run) plus a whitebox e2e over the ten required examples and an **integrated** wheel-throughput measurement. That measurement is the scheduling acceptance that probe 6 only estimated. | L2–L5 |

L1 starts alone. L2 and L5 can then run in parallel, then L3 and L4, then L6. There are no circular dependencies and no overlaps. Each leaf's files are announced to #19515 (Sophie) and #19643 (Vega) before it branches.

Newly visible at the estimate: 0. Newly mounted at the estimate: 0 ordinary, 21–23 of 49–54 fast. The estimate is read from the worker's geometry; 3 runs | None |

### Stage 4 — Prescription Layer

⚠️ **One prescription detail must go into L2.** "A block text container" is not enough inside today's cell: `.neo-grid-cell` is `display: flex`. A block child of a flex container is a flex item, and its automatic minimum width is its min-content width, i.e. its longest word. So `overflow-wrap: break-word` would still never break a long word, and the line overflows instead of wrapping. That is exactly probe 2's flex failure ([18879388](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19645#discussioncomment-18879388)), which a block *cell* fixed (0 misses).

In this mode L2 must therefore either make the cell `display: block`, or give the text container `min-width: 0` (and `flex: 1 1 auto`). L2 should also carry a spec in which a word longer than the column width still breaks.

Everything else is in the right layer:
- geometry in the App Worker grid owners;
- measurement through the existing `DomAccess` remote;
- the hidden subtree is VDom the grid renders, so no new main-thread addon is needed;
- no service boundary is crossed.

### Stage 5 — Avoided Traps Completeness

⚠️ Two traps to add; neither blocks:
- **A hidden subtree with `display: none`, or detached nodes,** has no layout box, so it measures 0. Use `visibility: hidden` inside the grid's scope. The Discussion has this, but the epic body doesn't say it.
- **No per-row main-thread `ResizeObserver` that writes heights.** The App Worker owns geometry, and a main-thread observer that writes would race the VDom and the pinning addon. Main reports observations only.

---

**Review verdict:** Greenlight. The design and mapping pass. Execution starts once L1–L6 are filed and linked; I'm filing them now. The Stage 4 and Stage 5 items become L2/L3 acceptance criteria.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-10-12T23:07:36Z

**Steward note: a browser limit on extents.**

The body's extent figure, about 4.8M px for 100k rows, assumed a 48px mean. #19666's example measures a mean of about 87px once #19663 learns it, which puts its extent at 8.7M px.

Above 2^23 px (8,388,608), headless Chrome rounds `scrollTop` to 2px, and above 2^24 to 4px. Measured on Google Chrome 155.0.8059.39, headless at DPR 1, through the e2e config's `channel: 'chrome'`. (Corrected: an earlier version of this comment named the wrong browser build.)

| Assigned | Reads back |
|---|---|
| `8388609` | `8388610` |
| `8697741` | `8697742` |
| `16777217` | `16777216` |

So past 2^23 px, a row anchored during a height correction holds to within 1px, not exactly. I traced the case to `GridRowScrollPinning`, which assigns exactly the offset the App computed, and the browser rounds it. #19666's e2e allows the browser's quantum past 2^23 px and stays exact below it.

No engine change is planned for this. Avoiding the rounding would take scaled scrolling, which this epic leaves out of scope. It belongs in the content-sized docs as a known limit.

**Update, the same day:** the operator's guidance is to test dynamic row heights with at most 10k rows, because element height limits also differ between Chrome, Firefox and Safari. #19666's example now holds 10k records (about 0.9M px), and its e2e checks are exact again.

### Rationale

Every parent outcome has a merged L3 witness. The two remaining residuals are tracked elsewhere:
- #6858 owns `AnimateRows`' fixed-height breakage, which predates this epic.
- #19657 owns running the Brain-gated tier, where `PremeasureRowsNL` lives, on every Engine PR. Today that tier runs on dev pushes; the latest passed it 11/11. Its one red, `DockMotionNL`, is outside this epic.

The acceptance journey runs at 10k on the operator's guidance ([6134339160](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19658#issuecomment-6134339160)): past 2^23 px Chrome rounds scroll offsets to 2px, and browsers cap element heights at different limits. This closeout claims no exact-position behavior beyond that boundary, and scaled scrolling past 100k rows stays deferred.

#19674 also noted a pre-existing scrollbar-track mismatch in its Deltas. No outcome of this epic depends on it.
